## Verdict

Dorado costs least for a team of 18, at $162 per month. It is the only vendor whose minimum (10 seats) falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the seats it uses. Inkwell bills for 25 seats and Borealis for 50, well past the 18 people on the team.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $9 | 10 |
| Inkwell | $14 | 25 |
| Borealis | $19 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (18) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 10 is below 18, so 18 seats paid. 18 × $9 = **$162 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 25 exceeds 18, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. Seven unused seats, worth $98.
- **Borealis:** minimum 50 exceeds 18, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. Thirty-two unused seats, worth $608.

Dorado is $188 per month cheaper than Inkwell and $788 cheaper than Borealis — $2,256 and $9,456 over twelve months. Effective cost per actual user: Dorado $9.00, Inkwell $19.44, Borealis $52.78.

## Risks

Seat minimums drive this result, not per-seat rates, so the ranking is sensitive to headcount. Inkwell's penalty disappears at 25 people, but even then Dorado costs $225 against Inkwell's $350, so Dorado stays cheaper at any size on this list. Borealis does not reach its list rate until 50 seats and is not price-competitive in this range.

The price list gives per-seat rates and minimums and nothing else. Feature coverage, support tiers, limits and contract terms are unknown, so this says which vendor is cheaper, not which is the better buy.

All figures assume monthly billing as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts and onboarding fees are not in the source. Check whether minimums bind at signup or only at renewal, since a shrinking team would keep paying the floor.
